title: Friday, September 4, 2026

headline.title: The jobs number landed hot and the tape repriced the Fed inside three minutes. Between 7:26 and 7:33am CT, GLD fell from 409.88 to 402.35, TLT gave up its entire pre-print gain, and IWM dropped 1.49 points while SPY lost only 1.77. Gold is now −1.92% and sitting below Thursday's 408.54 low after a clean 2 Up yesterday — the single most decisive chart on the board this morning. Waller cracked the door open on a September hold on Thursday and knocked hike odds from ~63% to ~50%; this print pushed back.
headline.summary: The rally has not died — it has narrowed to one group. Semis are the only thing still green: MU +0.86%, AMD +0.95%, NVDA +0.97%, AMAT +2.27%, SNDK +1.16%. But even they are fading — AMAT was +3.61% and SNDK +3.02% before the number. Everything else is offered: TSLA −3.20% handing back Cybercab day, MSFT −0.53%, META −0.33%, GOOGL −0.33% (ex-dividend today), and IWM −0.50% leading the downside as small caps take the rate hit first. LULU is −20.03% at 97.38 after cutting FY guidance to $9.48-9.73 from $13.26 — and the board's largest options ticket was already a $108.4M LULU $300P 12/18 block.

overview: Three minutes decided the morning. The August employment report printed hot enough that gold broke, and gold is the cleanest read on the difference between a fear day and a rates day — GLD 409.88 → 402.35 on the number, now −1.92% and, critically, under Thursday's 408.54 low after Thursday was a clean 2 Up. That is a failed 2 Up on the one chart that most directly prices the Fed. Underneath it the rotation is narrow and getting narrower: semis are the only green group (MU +0.86%, AMD +0.95%, AMAT +2.27%, NVDA +0.97%) and all of them are well off their pre-print marks. IWM −0.50% is the tell on the other side — small caps carry the most rate sensitivity and they are leading down, sitting right on Thursday's 293.43 low. Thursday's dark-pool board was already leaning this way: IVV $4.8B, VOO $3.1B and SPY $3.0B all cumulative ask, the whole index complex on one side into the print, with NVDA $1.7B bid the one big line still taking the other side. Markets are closed Monday for Labor Day, so today is a three-day-weekend close and positioning matters more than usual.
setups: Thursday was a clean 2 Up — H 413.54 / L 408.54, entirely above Wednesday's 403.33 high, closing 410.22. The jobs print took it straight through the bottom of that bar: 402.35, six dollars under Thursday's low, in three minutes. A 2 Up that loses its own low the next session is a failed 2 Up, and this one failed on the exact catalyst that defines the trade. Gold falling on a hot labour print is a real-yield move, not risk-off — the same signature that showed up on 9/1 when GLD fell 2.86% and GDX 3.90% into the 4.788% 10-year. Under 408.54 stays broken; a reclaim of it voids the whole thing.

Thursday was a genuine outside bar — H 959.76 over Wednesday's 958.00, L 918.88 under Wednesday's 927.16, closing 958.16 near the top of its own range. That is a 3 with a bullish resolution already implied by the close. Premarket 966.40 is above the 959.76 outside high, which is the trigger. The caution is that it printed 978.39 before the jobs number and has given back twelve dollars since, so the level is being tested rather than held. Over 959.76 is the setup; losing it puts the outside bar back in play in the other direction.

Thursday broke Wednesday's 452.36 low down to 440.50 and then closed 456.16, back above it — a textbook Failed 2 Down. Premarket 460.50 clears both Thursday's 459.77 high and Wednesday's 462.21 is the next one up. This is the cleanest of the semi setups because the reversal bar is already complete and the trigger sits just overhead rather than far below. Same caveat as MU: it was 464.59 pre-print. Over 459.77 confirms, 462.21 is the extension.

prep.lead: ⚠ Hot print, narrow tape, long weekend. Gold broke Thursday's low on the number and that is the highest-conviction chart on the board. Semis are the only green group and they are fading off their pre-print marks. IWM is sitting on 293.43 and small caps are leading down. Markets are closed Monday, so anything held today carries three days of headline risk with the FOMC two weeks out.

darkpool.note: Thursday's board leaned ask into the jobs print, and it leaned that way everywhere that matters. The single largest print on the whole tape was IVV $1.6B (ask, AH) — the second straight night IVV topped the board ask-side. On cumulative flow the entire index complex sat on one side: IVV $4.8B ask, VOO $3.1B ask, SPY $3.0B ask. The single-name top print also flipped: after NVDA and GOOGL bid prints led all week (NVDA $823M bid Wednesday, $761M bid Tuesday), Thursday's largest was META $618M (ask, AH). The one big line still drawing bid-side size was NVDA at $1.7B cumulative — and NVDA is the only mega-cap still green this morning, which is the single cleanest confirmation on the board. Two to discount: BAC $300M bid and PEP $269M bid both print with dividends hitting today, so some of that is mechanical rather than directional. One to watch: DELL $270M ask while sitting at an all-time high after a +15.8% Wednesday and a further run to 516.39 Thursday.
